methodology.title: 2.1 Core Principle: Future Aspirations
content: Problem: Students can describe the present and the past but struggle to articulate long-term goals and concrete plans for the future.

Solution: Introduce the distinction between "want to" (a desire or dream) and "going to" (a concrete plan). Students will frame their future careers using these structures, giving their graduation projects personal meaning.

games.materials: 10 sentence cards — 5 correct, 5 with errors based on: Future Tense: "want to" + verb / "going to" + verb

Fix-It: For error sentences, team that corrects fastest AND explains the rule earns double points.
Build: Each team member adds 1 original sentence using the grammar target. The chain must be logically connected — each sentence must link to the previous.

listening_script.text: What is the difference between a dream and a plan? Max says, "I want to be a pilot. That is my dream!" Luna says, "I am going to study aviation. That is my plan!" A dream is what you hope to achieve. A plan is what you are going to do to get there. "I want to become a teacher," says Mai. "So, I am going to read many books!" "I want to be a scientist," says Pip. "So, I am going to do experiments!" In the future, we will achieve our goals! We are going to work hard for our dreams!
